notes:
I couldn't write these notes because the research tool failed before I read any pages.

My first attempt to fetch the sources (Enduring Word, the Bible Hub pages for Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit and Wesley, and Precept Austin on Ezekiel 36) crashed on the very first page. My code didn't handle the format the fetch tool sent back. When I tried to rerun it, the system told me I had no more tool calls left for this turn. So I haven't read anything from any of the approved sites.

You asked me to report only what the pages say and to give a URL for every point, so I've left the notes empty rather than filling them from memory.

**If you send another message (even just "continue"), I can run the research again.** Here's the plan:

1. **Traditional verse-by-verse reading:**
   - enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-36/
   - Bible Hub's pages for Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit Commentary and Wesley's Notes on Ezekiel 36
   - Precept Austin's Ezekiel 36 page
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ**, mainly on vv. 25–27 (the clean water, new heart and Spirit):
   - Reformed and Baptist teachers on new birth coming before faith: Ligonier, Desiring God, GTY, Monergism
   - Lutheran teachers on baptism (LCMS, 1517)
   - Wesleyan teachers on entire sanctification (wesley.nnu.edu, Seedbed)
   - Pentecostal teachers on the Spirit (Enduring Word, AG)
   - Views on Israel's future return to the land in vv. 24–28, from GotQuestions and Bible.org
3. **Other views:**
   - NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship
   - Catholic.com and New Advent on v. 25 and baptism
   - OCA for the Orthodox reading
   - Prosperity or word-of-faith uses of vv. 29–30 and 37, only if the approved sites discuss them
